neighbours.label: the superlative suffix piece split from an adjective stem (blood|iest, snow|iest, storm|iest)
fire: It was the bloodiest battle of the entire war.
Last January was the snowiest month on record in Boston.
Chicago is not actually the windiest city in America.
This is the rainiest week we have had all year.
That was the stormiest crossing the ferry crew could remember.
Our trail was the muddiest after the spring floods.
He picked the spiciest dish on the menu.
She told the funniest story at the dinner party.
quiet: It was a bloody battle in the middle of the war.
Last January was a snowy month in Boston.
Chicago is a windy city in America.
This has been a rainy week for us.
That was a stormy crossing for the ferry crew.
Our trail was muddy after the spring floods.
He picked a spicy dish from the menu.
She told a funny story at the dinner party.

notes: Card peaks: iest x7, ier x5, hest, est. Checked tokenization: bloodiest, snowiest, windiest, rainiest, stormiest split stem+'iest'. Near misses use the base adjective.
